blurb: Low-slung scent hound with long ears and a nose second only to the Bloodhound
description: The Basset Hound is a short-legged, heavy-boned scent hound of French descent with long ears, loose skin and a mild, friendly, devoted temperament.
answer: The Basset Hound is a short-legged scent hound descended from French basset types and developed further in Britain to hunt rabbit and hare on foot. It stands about 33–38 cm but is heavy for its height, and is described as friendly, mild and devoted.

body: Basset-type dogs trace back to the hounds of St Hubert and were first mentioned in a French hunting text in 1585. Short legs let hunters follow on foot rather than on horseback. The name comes from the French bas, meaning low. Bassets became fashionable under Napoleon III and were shown at the first Paris dog exhibition in 1863.

French bassets reached England by the 1870s. In the 1890s Everett Millais, regarded as the father of the modern breed, crossed one with a Bloodhound to create a heavier dog. The first standard was drawn up in Britain at the end of the nineteenth century and updated in 2010.

The Basset Hound is built like a large dog on short legs, and relative to its size it is heavier-boned than any other breed. Weight varies between bloodlines, commonly 20–35 kg. Loose, wrinkled skin, a dewlap and long ears that help stir up ground scent give it its sad look. The short coat comes in hound colors, most often tricolor or red and white, but not merle or brindle.

The breed is commonly described as friendly, outgoing and playful, tolerant of children and other pets, and mild and devoted without being timid. As a scent hound it was bred to follow a trail persistently.

Sources give little specific care guidance. As a hound bred for steady hunting on foot, it is generally thought to benefit from regular walks and chances to use its nose, and its long ears and skin folds may need routine checking.

The short stature results from osteochondrodysplasia. Conditions reported in the breed include gastric dilatation volvulus, primary open-angle glaucoma, an inherited platelet disorder, yeast infections and skin problems such as allergic skin disease, intertrigo, Malassezia dermatitis and otitis. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years.

faq.q: How big does a Basset Hound get?
faq.a: It stands about 33–38 cm at the withers but is heavily built, with weights varying by bloodline, commonly in the 20–35 kg range.

faq.q: How long do Basset Hounds live?
faq.a: Lifespan is usually given as about 10–12 years; a 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years.

faq.q: Are Basset Hounds good with children?
faq.a: The breed is commonly described as friendly and tolerant of children and other pets, with a mild, devoted nature.
